title: Allergic load and symptom severity in children with tic disorders: a cross-sectional study
novelty: Absent from prior scan returns and current evidence ledger; first published before prior run, newly encountered today. Cause/timing of query-membership change unresolved.
population: Children with tic disorders aged 4–13; investigators affiliated with Fujian Children's Hospital, China. Recruitment details unverified.
comparator: Tic-disorder group without associated allergic disease
exposure: Composite allergic-load index integrating total IgE, specific-IgE item count and allergic-disease count; exact construction/weighting and regression adjustment unverified.
outcome: YGTSS total-tic score, range 0–50; group comparisons include separately described functional impairment.
followup: No longitudinal follow-up verified; cross-sectional design
attrition: Publisher's public data-availability statement describes complete-case YGTSS/allergy analysis without imputation; excluded/incomplete counts not verified.
adverse_events: Not a treatment trial; no treatment safety estimate extracted.
risk_of_bias: Temporal order and causality unidentified; possible confounding, recruitment/complete-case selection and measurement effects. Adjustment, multiplicity, precision and cohort overlap require methods verification.
conflicts_funding: Authors report no competing interests. Publisher lists Fujian grants 2025J011209 and 2024Y9564 and reports no funder role.
applicability: Pediatric association only; no persistent-severe-adult estimate, treatment comparison or externally validated prediction.
cohort_overlap_status: Unverified; do not call independent replication.
claim_supported: Higher composite allergy load is associated with higher tic severity in the analyzed children.
claim_not_supported: Allergy causes tics; allergy treatment improves tics; individual prediction, adult generalization, durable benefit, disease modification or cure.
retrieval_status: PubMed abstract/date XML and publicly accessible publisher overview/metadata, data availability and declarations inspected. Main methods/tables inaccessible in this pass; linked supplement not inspected. No paper copied into package.
reviewer: Research assistant source extraction; not independent clinical peer review
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in PubMed; focused date-filtered notice query zero. Not a complete publisher-history audit.
next_verification_task: Verify lawful methods/supplement for adjustment, index definition, intervals, selection and cohort overlap before any further inference.
